title: a render ran out of VRAM inside ComfyUI (torch OOM)
evidence: 1 ComfyUI torch-OOM(s) in the last 48h; newest comfyui-comfyui-1789999255-213957-1.log (25.3h old); died at 21.32 GiB allocated, 78.00 MiB requested, device limit 23.52 GiB; the budget was 21719.11 MB usable / 21448.72 MB loaded; launch args for THAT log: NONE -- that start carried no --reserve-vram (its launch line has no args=, i.e. the process predates the flag); the 5 launch(es) since held the budget at <= 16896 MB usable. This is the CAUSE of the HTTP-500 / timeout rows tracked as render-execution-error: ComfyUI sizes its dynamic-VRAM budget from FREE memory, so the emptier the card the MORE it loads -- over-committing is fatal, offloading is merely slower. Compare the failing budget ONLY against the launch args named above, which are read from the launch line of the SAME log that carries the OOM -- an older start's budget says nothing about a newer launch's flags. Two questions, in order: (1) did that start carry --reserve-vram (bin/comfyui_harness.sh COMFY_RESERVE_VRAM) at all? (2) if it did and 'usable' still sits at the failing value, the flag did not reach the budget -- check comfy_aimdo's simple_vram_headroom path against the runtime .venv (/mnt/fscache/essdee/ComfyUI/.venv, comfy_aimdo 0.5.5 accepts it; the sibling venv/ holds 0.4.3 and silently falls back). Self-closes when no OOM is inside the window.

notes.note: 2026-09-22 05:4xZ ops-triage: DECISION -- accept the measured throughput cost of --reserve-vram 5 and keep the value. New primary evidence (comfyui_jobs created_at/completed_at pairs): renders ran 261s (7565) and 304s (7567) BEFORE the reserve, 412s (7568) and 402s (7569) AFTER it -- the ~6.2 GB of extra offload costs ~110-140s per render. That now overruns the growth tick: its producer budget is SYNC_BUDGET_SECONDS=360 and its foreground tool call is SIGKILLed at ~420s, so a ~410s render consumes the whole window and the tick's OWN post-actions (import/caption/slot) are routinely killed. Evidence: PipelineRuns 480/482/483/484 were each marked failed by the reconciler with the honest reason 'sync producer Growth::ContentGenerator left this run non-terminal with no job in flight (the producer process was killed before it wrote a terminal status)'. CONTENT IS NOT LOST: Growth::AbandonedRenderWorker (armed in the always-on sidekiq; verified this pass -- exactly 1 job of that class in Sidekiq::ScheduledSet, next 05:39:00Z) recovered posts 349/350/351 at 03:44/04:48Z. WHY ACCEPT: (i) lowering COMFY_RESERVE_VRAM leaves ~20.9 GB usable against the 21.7 GB budget line that was fatal, re-risking the OOM the flag exists to prevent; (ii) the queue is AT TARGET (publishable=21, dry_out 2026-09-28T14:00Z) so recovery latency costs no content; (iii) a killed tick costs one render window, not a render. REVERSAL TRIGGER (a threshold, not a vibe): queue below target or dry_out inside ~3 days, or 2 consecutive ticks whose completed render is still unrecovered past 60 min -- then fix the producer LAUNCH MODE (run it detached in its own cgroup so post-actions are not inside the caller's window), not the VRAM flag. Probe-owned: self-closes 48h after the last OOM (2026-09-24 ~00:05Z).

2026-09-22 06:3xZ ops-triage: TRIGGER CORRECTED against a measured counterexample -- the reversal trigger recorded in the 05:4xZ note ('queue below target or dry_out inside ~3 days') FIRES ON THE HEALTHY STEADY STATE and would have triggered a launch-mode change on a working system. Measured this pass: publishable=19 against target=21 at 06:11Z decomposes EXACTLY into 21 status_rows - 1 age-gate hold (post 345) - 1 due-but-paced post (329, held by scheduling:post_scheduled pacing: 'Pacing: holding 1 further due post(s) ... still due, releases on the next tick'), plus post 321 published at 06:00Z by the hourly publisher. A queue below target mid-hour is the NORMAL reading of a system that paces one release per tick and tops up one render per tick -- not evidence of starvation. CORRECTED TRIGGER (interval, not point): act only if (a) dry_out under 3 days, OR (b) the shortfall FAILS TO CLOSE across 2 or more consecutive hourly ticks (what closes it is the render+salvage pair: posts 348@02:01Z, 349/350@03:44Z, 351@04:48Z this window), OR (c) 2 or more ticks whose completed render is still unrecovered past 60 min. ALSO RECORDED, because that trigger named a fix already rejected: 'run the producer detached in its own cgroup' was DECIDED AGAINST (item growth-tick-launch-mode, closed 2026-09-21 11:22 -- 'This is a BUDGET rather than a detached launch on purpose: step 4 GPU release must run after the producer returns, so backgrounding it would let the shutdown SIGTERM ComfyUI mid-render'). DECISION UNCHANGED: keep --reserve-vram 5, no change.

ACCEPTANCE HOLDS, now with a longer track record -- the --reserve-vram 5 fix has survived 5 consecutive renders with zero OOM: ComfyuiJob 7568 (415s), 7569 (402s), 7570 (723s under co-tenant pressure), 7571 (406s), 7572 (354s), all status=completed between 02:42Z and 07:07Z on 09-22; no torch.OutOfMemoryError anywhere in log/development.log since the 00:05Z pair, and the budget line stays in the proven envelope (usable ~13.5-16.9 GB vs the FATAL 21719.11 MB). The throughput cost accepted at 05:4xZ is unchanged (400-720s per render vs 256-304s before the reserve). No new decision needed; probe-owned (48h window, newest OOM 09-22 00:0xZ) so it self-closes ~09-24 00:01Z. The corrected reversal trigger from 06:3xZ stands: act only on dry_out under 3 days, or a shortfall that fails to close across 2+ consecutive hourly ticks, or 2+ ticks whose completed render is still unrecovered past 60 min.

2026-09-22 09:4xZ ops-triage: ACCEPTANCE VERIFIED BY THE DISCRIMINATOR rather than by a render count. Launch-args history in log/comfyui_harness.log: the OOM log (comfyui-comfyui-1789999255-213957-1.log, last write 00:19:09Z) belongs to the 00:00:53Z launch, which carries NO --reserve-vram; --reserve-vram 5 first appears at 02:34:22Z and EVERY launch since (02:34Z, 03:00Z, 04:01Z, 06:00Z, 07:01Z) carries it, with zero OOMs after it. The flag is the discriminator and it holds. Nothing unactioned; probe-owned, self-closes ~09-24 00:01Z once the 00:19Z event leaves the 48h window. The corrected reversal trigger from 06:3xZ stands.

2026-09-22 18:5xZ ops-triage: the accepted fix had a HOLE, now closed -- filed, fixed and closed as comfyui-adoption-bypasses-reserve (read it for the evidence; commit follows). Short version: --reserve-vram 5 is on every launch line WE write, but bin/comfyui_harness.sh ADOPTS any instance already answering :8188 instead of relaunching, so a co-tenant's un-reserved instance (live now: pid 3662070, tmux scope, reserve=missing) would have run our workflow at a card-sized budget. cmd_ensure now refuses to render through a ComfyUI whose /proc/<pid>/cmdline lacks the flag, before requesting a claim, and status reports reserve=<ok|missing>. Verified live (refusal logged, rc=2, scheduler events.log unchanged) and offline (bin/comfyui_harness_test.sh ALL PASS, +8 assertions including the negative control that a FLAGGED instance is still adopted). ACCEPTANCE UNCHANGED: --reserve-vram 5 stays, no flag change; the throughput trade and the 09-24 ~00:01Z self-close window are unaffected. ALSO RECORDED, because the armed reversal trigger named a remedy that was already rejected: 'run the producer detached in its own cgroup' was DECIDED AGAINST (growth-tick-launch-mode, closed 2026-09-21 11:22 -- step 4's GPU release must run after the producer returns). CORRECTED REMEDY LADDER for when the trigger DOES fire (dry_out under 3 days, or a shortfall that fails to close across 2+ consecutive hourly ticks, or 2+ ticks with a completed render unrecovered past 60 min): (1) read the harness log for WHICH refusal it is -- 'vram_insufficient' (card genuinely too full) vs the new reserve-guard line (a foreign un-reserved instance is up); (2) do NOT lower COMFY_RESERVE_VRAM and do NOT lower VRAM_MIN_FIT -- both re-risk the over-commit this item exists for, and a smaller budget also makes the render slower than the growth tick's 360s budget, so it cannot complete inside a tick anyway; (3) do NOT touch the foreign instance; (4) the only lever we do not own is the GPU itself, so at dry_out under 3 days route a tim item (GPU policy, which the loop's scope explicitly allows) carrying the holder evidence (pid/cgroup/args/hours held/free MiB) and the dry-out date -- until then the queue absorbs the skipped windows.

2026-09-22 20:0xZ ops-triage: no new event -- the 48h window still holds exactly the one 00:05Z OOM (19.7h old), and the --reserve-vram 5 acceptance is untouched because nothing has rendered since 07:01Z. New and relevant: the card is now held by an ACTIVE foreign batch that our pipeline refuses to adopt WITHOUT the flag (proved from comfy/model_management.py: budget = freshly freed memory - extra_reserved, so unflagged lands ~22.1GiB = the fatal case, flagged ~17.5GiB = the proven envelope). That refusal is the fix working as designed, not a regression. Probe-owned, self-closes ~09-24 00:01Z; corrected remedy ladder recorded 18:5xZ stands.
